raw.translational: Understanding the shared genetic basis of these conditions highlights the critical role of V(D)J recombination in immune development. Therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring RAG complex function or compensating for its deficiency could potentially benefit patients with either disease. Gene therapy approaches targeting hematopoietic stem cells to restore functional RAG1 or RAG2 could offer a cure.

partners.mechanism_chain: RAG2 (HGNC:9832) —DISRUPTS→ V(D)J recombination; RAG1 (HGNC:9831) —DISRUPTS→ V(D)J recombination; V(D)J recombination —LEADS_TO→ Combined immunodeficiency (HP:0002704); V(D)J recombination —LEADS_TO→ Skin granulomas (HP:0003497); RAG2 (HGNC:9832) —LEADS_TO→ Recombinase activating gene 2 deficiency (MONDO:0000573). Loss-of-function mutations in either RAG1 or RAG2 disrupt the V(D)J recombination pathway, which is essential for adaptive immune receptor gene assembly. This disruption leads to a combined immunodeficiency (affecting both T and B cell lineages) and can manifest with phenotypes such as skin granulomas. The direct genetic cause of recombinase activating gene 2 deficiency (MONDO:0000573) is a defect in RAG2, which is a component of the V(D)J recombination machinery.

partners.mechanism_chain: Variant in IL2RG (HGNC:6078) —DISRUPTS→ IL2RG (HGNC:6078); IL2RG (HGNC:6078) —DECREASES→ Common gamma chain cytokine signaling (GO:0038273); Common gamma chain cytokine signaling (GO:0038273) —LEADS_TO→ Combined immunodeficiency (HP:0002694); Common gamma chain cytokine signaling (GO:0038273) —LEADS_TO→ Skin granulomas (HP:0030043); Common gamma chain cytokine signaling (GO:0038273) —LEADS_TO→ X-linked combined immunodeficiency (MONDO:0010730). Variants in IL2RG disrupt the common gamma chain, leading to impaired cytokine signaling essential for lymphocyte development and function, manifesting as combined immunodeficiency.
